rv.q: City Lit Theater in Chicago has reincarnated 'Shane' into an extraordinary and psychologically riveting stage play, and it compares favorably to the film.

It is a thoughtful meditation on what it means to 'be a man.' A strong cast and some first-class fight choreography help bring this story to life, and it should definitely be on your list of Chicago theater to see this fall.
This is a good production of a classic American story. But what really makes it worth seeing is Woods as Shane.
It's a gripping story; not for nothing has it been adapted multiple times... Pracht pulls it off for the most part, finding nuance in unexpected places and shading his characters beautifully.
As the titular mysterious drifter, Michael B. Woods is outstanding, conveying from the beginning Shane's constant struggle against his past as a killer.
The strong performances, impressive fight choreography, and detailed worldbuilding make the story engaging from beginning to end.
City Lit's Shane is earnest, capable entry for anyone looking to step into the Wild West for an evening.
Pracht's retelling of this tale is done with finesse.
With stage combat, gunshots, a mysterious stranger, and a fight for the land they call home, Shane has all the hallmarks of a classic Western.
But this is an excellent theater company, a fine director, so manifestly there's a reason for this seemingly limited point of view...
